plan.title: Treatment x time interaction DE in 2x4 time course
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question — which genes change specifically with treatment beyond the shared time trend — is a treatment x time interaction question on a 2 conditions x 4 time points x 3 replicates bulk RNA-seq design (counts.csv, 12000 genes x 24 sample columns plus the gene-symbol column; metadata.csv, 24 rows with condition, time, time_hours). The primary test is therefore a DESeq2 likelihood ratio test of the full model ~ condition + time + condition:time against the reduced model ~ condition + time, which is the correct test when the interaction spans several coefficients (4 time points => 3 interaction coefficients) and makes no assumption about the shape of the trajectory. A Wald test on a single interaction coefficient would answer only 'does the treatment effect at time t differ from that at t0', not the full question.

T1S1 does sample-structure QC on blind VST (PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes) coloured by condition and time, to check that the time axis and the condition axis are visible and that no replicate is misplaced, before any model runs. T1S2 fits the LRT on genes with at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples (the smallest cell size), keeps DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization inside the model, sets explicit reference levels (condition reference and time = t0), and reports BH-adjusted p-values at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering plus a p-value histogram. T1S3 turns the significant interaction genes into interpretable trajectories: per-time-point log2 fold changes of treated vs control (each shrunken with apeglm/ashr as appropriate), clustering of those profiles, and the simple effects at each time point reported beside the interaction result. T2S1 runs preranked fgsea on the full tested list — ranked by the signed LRT-derived statistic — against the human MSigDB Hallmark collection, then GO BP as the second collection, since the Reactome C2 subset is not staged in this environment (Hallmark and GO BP/CC/MF are; WikiPathways human is also present as a further follow-up). T1S4 assembles the report with the fit diagnostics, the interaction and simple-effect tables, the leading-edge genes, and an explicit power statement.

Power is the central caveat and the plan states it rather than working around it: 3 replicates per cell is low, and an interaction coefficient is a difference of differences whose standard error exceeds that of a main effect at the same replicate count. Absence from the interaction list is not evidence that a gene responds identically in both conditions. Thresholds stay at their defaults; no loosening to manufacture hits.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes
Keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples (smallest cell size)
~ condition + time + condition:time with explicit reference levels (condition reference = control, time reference = t0)
DESeq2 likelihood ratio test, full ~ condition + time + condition:time vs reduced ~ condition + time
apeglm log fold change shrinkage on individual interaction coefficients
fgsea preranked GSEA on the LRT-derived ranked list with MSigDB Hallmark then GO BP
Interaction report: trajectory clusters, simple effects and interaction contrasts side by side, MA and dispersion plots, power statement, reproducibility record

steps.name: Preranked GSEA on the interaction signal
steps.question: Which biological processes are enriched among the genes whose time profile differs between the two conditions?
steps.description: Rank every gene tested in T1S2 (not a thresholded subset) and run fgsea preranked against the human MSigDB Hallmark collection, then against human GO Biological Process as the second collection. Ranking metric: the signed LRT statistic — the LRT statistic carries no direction, so sign it by the treated-vs-control shrunken log2FC at the last time point (t3), and state this construction explicitly in the output; report the unsigned-LRT ranking as a sensitivity check. Use a gene set size window of 15 to 500 after intersecting each set with the tested genes, BH adjustment, and a fixed random seed for the permutations. Map gene symbols to the collection identifier space and report the share of tested genes that failed to map. Collapse redundant significant sets (fgsea collapsePathways) and report one representative per group with the full table as a supplement, plus the leading-edge genes of each significant set with their gene-level statistic.
steps.context: Reference data needed: human hallmark gene sets, and a human GO biological process gene set collection, both keyed on HGNC symbols — the same identifier space as the counts matrix. Both are present in this environment (MSigDB 2026.1 hallmark human and C5 GO BP human), as is a human WikiPathways GMT for a further follow-up. The Reactome C2 subset that the standard procedure names as the second collection is NOT staged here; GO BP substitutes for it and the substitution must be stated in the output. If a named collection is absent at run time, report which one and continue with those present.

The ranking metric is stated exactly, including how the unsigned LRT statistic was given a direction, and the unsigned-LRT sensitivity run is reported
Gene set size window 15-500 applied after intersection with the tested genes
Both the hallmark collection and the GO BP collection are run, each with its file version recorded; the absence of Reactome C2 and the substitution of GO BP are stated
Share of tested genes that failed to map to the collection identifier space is reported
Redundant significant sets are collapsed and one representative per group is reported, with the full table kept as a supplement
Leading-edge genes with their gene-level statistics are listed for each significant set, and overlaps of leading edges between reported sets are marked
The permutation seed is recorded
constraints: enrichment: gsea_input = full_ranked_list; universe = tested genes
enrichment: min_size = 15, max_size = 500 after intersection
enrichment: collapse_redundant = TRUE

enrichment: gene identifiers stay in one space — the GMTs are HGNC symbols and the counts matrix is HGNC symbols, so map only if a collection requires it, and never mix spaces between the list and the sets

Disputed ranking metric (R-0108): this plan chooses the test statistic scaled by its uncertainty (the LRT statistic, signed by the t3 shrunken log2FC) over the signed -log10 p-value and over the shrunken fold change alone, and states the choice in the report
Do not run an over-representation test if fewer than ~50 genes pass padj<0.05; the ranked method on the full list is the method either way
Set and record a random seed for the fgsea permutations

GO BP is a nested hierarchy, so significant hits arrive in correlated blocks — collapse before counting them as findings

steps.name: Interaction report with power statement
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to 'which genes show a treatment-specific change over the four time points beyond the shared time trend', and what are the limits of that answer at 3 replicates per cell?
steps.description: Assemble the final report from T1S2, T1S3 and T2S1. State first: the method (DESeq2 LRT, full ~ condition + time + condition:time vs reduced ~ condition + time), the package versions, the design and the reference levels, the thresholds (padj<0.05, BH, independent filtering), the number of genes tested after filtering, and the number of significant interaction genes. Present the fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram) before the gene tables. Then the interaction gene table with, per gene, the interaction LRT statistic and padj, the simple effect at each time point, the unshrunken and shrunken log2FC with lfcSE, and the trajectory cluster. Then the trajectory cluster figures. Then the enrichment section: collections and their versions, the ranking metric and how it was signed, the universe, the size window, the collapsed representative sets, and the leading-edge genes. Close with an explicit power statement: 3 replicates per cell, an interaction is a difference of differences with an inflated standard error, benchmark studies at n=3 recover only a minority of true differentially expressed genes and mostly those with large fold changes, therefore absence from the interaction list is not evidence of an identical response in the two conditions. Attach the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, all package versions, the permutation seed, and the gene set collection file versions.
steps.context: Consolidation step. Everything reported must trace to an artifact produced by T1S2, T1S3 or T2S1 — no numbers are to be recomputed or estimated here.
acceptance_criteria: Method, package versions, design formula, reference levels, thresholds, number of genes tested and number of significant genes appear before the gene tables
MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histogram are included as fit diagnostics
Interaction contrast and simple effects at each time point are shown side by side per gene, with the reference level of each factor named
Both unshrunken and shrunken log2FC with lfcSE appear in the gene table, and ranking is on the shrunken value
Trajectory clusters are reported with their method, count and mean profiles
Enrichment section states collection names and versions, ranking metric and its signing, universe, size window, and lists leading-edge genes per representative set, with the method-dependence caveat
An explicit power statement at 3 replicates per cell is present, stating that absence from the list is not evidence of no effect
Reproducibility record attached: sessionInfo, package versions, seed, collection versions
No claim in the report lacks a supporting artifact from an upstream step
constraints: Report only what upstream steps produced; recompute nothing
State the deviation from the default Wald interaction test (LRT chosen because 4 time points give 3 interaction coefficients) and the absence of a staged Reactome collection
Do not present the enrichment sets as established mechanism
caveats: A second DE method (edgeR quasi-likelihood with the same design) would give a robustness overlap; it is not planned as a separate step, and the report should note that only one test framework was run rather than imply cross-method agreement
